text:
oliver: heads up — getting a flood of NCCL watchdog alerts in us-west after the driver rollout to 535.x. ops-bot posted a bunch of alerts around 11:05UTC. anyone else seeing this pattern?
ops-bot: ALERT: metric nccl_watchdog.count > 25 on cluster=redwood-us-west-2 (5m). Affected nodes: gpu-pool-{12..18}.link to alert: https://grafana.redwood/alerts/9832 :warning:
oliver: here's one of the logs from node gpu-pool-14:
```
Mar 18 11:04:23 gpu-node kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, PID=2731, GPU has fallen off the bus
Mar 18 11:04:23 gpu-node kernel: nvidia: GPU 0000:65:00.0: GPU has fallen off the bus.
Mar 18 11:04:23 gpu-node systemd: Started NVIDIA Persistence Daemon.
```
maria: Xid 79 = GPU hang/fall off bus in our experience. We saw something similar with driver 525->530 last year but those were tied to a kernel ABI mismatch on older EC2 AMIs. Have we pinned kernels on these nodes?
raj: checking node image versions now — looks like nodes in that pool are on ami-2023-09-15 (kernel 5.15.0-102) while the driver package was built against 6.1 headers. mismatch likely.
sre-oncall: good catch. immediate mitigations: 1) cordon+drain affected nodes from the GPU pool, 2) scale up spare pool to avoid throttling user traffic, 3) roll the driver on one node with the older kernel to confirm repro, 4) if reproducible, roll back driver to 530 until we build a compat release. Runbook ref: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/gpu-driver-regressions
ken: adding the quick commands here — caution: destructive if used wrong:
```
# cordon + drain
kubectl cordon gpu-node-14 -n inference
kubectl drain gpu-node-14 -n inference --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# restart driver
ssh gpu-node-14 'sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced || sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia'
# check XIDs
ssh gpu-node-14 'nvidia-smi -q -d ERRORS | grep -A3 Xid'
```
maria: also let's enable NCCL async error handling as a short-term safety valve on deployments that can handle transient retries: set env NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1 on the failing pods. It won't fix the root cause but can reduce customer-facing failures while we investigate.
ops-bot: NOTE: autoscaler has started two on-demand instances to compensate for drained nodes — estimated 3.8k USD/day if not stabilized. :money_with_wings:
raj: creating a 1hr patch window to test kernel rebuild + driver 535 on a single canary node. I'll post results. If it fails we should trigger rollback.
sre-oncall: monitoring checklist I'm adding to the alert: add metric nccl_watchdog.rate, xids_by_code (grouped), and node_gpu_fell_off_bus boolean. Alert policy: warn at >5 nodes in 10m, page at >15 nodes in 5m.
oliver: can we also add log sampling for `dmesg` around the time of the Xid? those traces are helpful for vendor escalation.
ken: opened ticket INF-7721 and attached logs + timeline. Also pinged nv-support with kernel+driver combos.
maria: if nv-support suggests kernel patch, coordinate with images team — rolling AMIs takes time. For now, recommend pinning driver to 530 in Dedicated pools and throttling new 535 rollouts.
raj: can confirm: reinstalling driver 530 on node-14 cleared the Xid 79s after a warm reboot. Will run more checks.
sre-oncall: thanks. follow-ups: 1) add a short runbook step to confirm kernel-driver ABI compatibility before auto-rollout, 2) add a dashboard tile showing driver version vs kernel version heatmap, 3) add an automated preflight check in the canary pipeline. I'll create follow-up tickets.
oliver: perfect — please post the rollback plan and ETA here once ready. tagging @maria @raj @ken for action. :thumbsup:
